newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CRUZ HITS GAME-WINNING HOMER IN BLUE JAYS DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CRUZ HITS GAME-WINNING HOMER IN BLUE JAYS DEBUT.

text.p: Thursday's deal that brought Jose Cruz Jr to the Blue Jays from Seattle paid immediate dividends for Toronto Friday.
In his Blue Jays debut, Cruz smacked a two-run homer in a three-run sixth inning as Toronto snapped a six-game losing streak with a 7-5 victory over the Detroit Tigers.
Cruz smacked a 2-1 offering from Dan Miceli (2-2) over the right-field wall to give Toronto a 6-5 lead.

"He certainly came up with a big home run for us," Blue Jays manager Cito Gaston said. "We had some big hits tonight, some that we have been looking for just about all year, and I hope we can keep it going."
Otis Nixon, Joe Carter and Alex Gonzalez also homered for the Blue Jays.
Tony Clark had a solo homer and Raul Casanova belted a three-run shot off Pat Hentgen in a four-run fourth that put Detroit in front 5-3.
Hentgen (11-7) picked up the win despite allowing five runs and nine hits over 7 1/3 innings.
In New York, Andy Pettitte came within one out of his fifth complete game and the Yankees pounded out 14 hits in an 8-3 victory over the Minnesota Twins.
Pettitte (13-6) gave up just three runs -- on homers to Terry Steinbach and Chuck Knoblauch -- despite allowing a career-high 13 hits.
New York batted around the order in the fourth inning, scoring five runs on five hits.
Bernie Williams, who returned to the New York lineup for the first time since going on the disabled list June 15 with a hamstring injury, had two hits, including an RBI double.
In Kansas City, Mo Vaughn had four hits and drove in a pair of runs and Mike Stanley added a two-run homer as the Boston Red Sox routed the Royals 10-3.
Steve Avery (5-2) and two relievers combined on a seven-hitter as the Red Sox won for the first time in Kansas City in a year.
Wil Cordero added three hits as Boston pounded out 15 hits, including nine against Royals starter Jose Rosado (7-8).
Stanley homered in the first, Vaughn added his 25th in the third and Nomar Garciaparra had a solo shot in the fourth -- all off Rosado.

In Milwaukee, the Brewers ran their winning streak to nine as Jeromy Burnitz's two-run homer highlighted a six-run second inning and Cal Eldred allowed two runs over seven strong innings in an 8-3 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
The nine straight wins are the most for the Brewers since a 10-game streak in 1988.

Burnitz hit a 1-2 pitch from Bob Wolcott (5-5) over the wall in right field for a 2-0 lead. Jesse Levis, Fernando Vina and Jeff Cirillo added RBI singles and Dave Nilsson's grounder plated Vina to cap the big inning.
Eldred (11-10) retired the first 10 batters he faced and pitched 5 2/3 no-hit innings.

At Texas, Matt Williams homered twice and Omar Vizquel's run-scoring single snapped an eighth-inning tie as the Cleveland Indians stopped a four-game losing streak with an 8-5 victory over the Rangers.
Williams belted his 24th homer in the fourth inning and added number 25, another sholo shot, in the eighth. Tony Fernandez, Jim Thome (28) and Manny Ramirez also homered for the Indians.

Jose Mesa (2-4) allowed a hit and walked two in two scoreless innings for the win. Eric Gunderson (2-1) suffered his second blown save as he allowed two runs and two hits while recording only one out for the loss.
In Anaheim, Allen Watson allowed one run over eight innings and Tim Salmon had two hits and four RBI as the Angels routed the Chicago White Sox 9-1.
The win moved the Angels past Seattle into sole possession of first place in the AL West.
Watson (9-6) allowed eight hits and three walks, while striking out seven.

It was the sixth game of the season with at least four RBI for Salmon, who is 41-for-104 (.394) with 36 RBI in his last 28 games. Darin Erstad added two hits, including his 11th homer, scored three times and had three RBI for the Angels.

In Oakland, Matt Stairs's single down the right-field line scored pinch-runner Steve Karsay with the winning run as the Athletics broke a six-game losing streak with a 2-1 victory over the Baltimore Orioles.
T.J. Mathews (1-0), acquired Thursday from the Cardinals for slugger Mark McGwire, gave up two hits while retiring five batters to win his American League debut.
Baltimore, which saw its seven-game winning streak halted, got its lone run on Geronimo Berroa's two-out homer in the sixth.
